message.content: Let's wire Eve's copilot panel to pi-ai. I want streaming responses in the side panel, and a `draw_shape` tool the model can call to drop elements onto the Excalidraw canvas. Route is app/api/copilot/route.ts, the panel is components/CopilotPanel.tsx. Keep it provider-agnostic — we may swap Anthropic for OpenAI later.

content.text: Got it. The plan: the route streams from pi-ai's unified API and forwards events to the panel over an SSE response; `draw_shape` is a pi-ai tool whose calls we replay against the canvas store. Provider stays behind pi-ai so the swap is a one-line config change later. Let me read the current stub and how the panel consumes it.

Stub as expected. pi-ai exposes `streamSimple` for the common case and emits typed events (`text_delta`, `tool_call`, `tool_call_delta`, `stop`). I'll define the `draw_shape` tool with a JSON schema, stream text deltas straight through, and accumulate tool-call partial JSON until `stop` so the final args are never truncated.

Good — the client is already centralized in lib/ai.ts with usage tracking, so the route just consumes it. Writing the handler now: define the tool, open a stream, pipe deltas to a ReadableStream, and emit a final `tool_call` event with the assembled draw_shape arguments.
Now the panel side: it needs to read the SSE stream, append text deltas to the transcript, and when a `tool_call` for draw_shape arrives, call the canvas store's addElement. Reading the panel.

Replacing send() with an SSE reader: parse each `data:` frame, switch on event type, append text_delta to the streaming assistant message, and on a draw_shape tool_call call useCanvas().addElement({ type: kind, x, y, label }). I'll keep a ref to the in-flight message so deltas land on the right bubble.

content.content: applied: streaming send() via EventSource reader; draw_shape → canvas.addElement

message.content: Make sure the tool call streams incrementally and the final draw_shape args aren't dropped when the model stops — that bit me last time.

content.text: That's the decision that matters here: pi-ai delivers tool arguments as `tool_call_delta` partial-JSON chunks and only the `stop` event guarantees they're complete. So I accumulate the raw string and JSON.parse on stop, not per-delta. The canvas mutation fires once, after stop. There's a known pi-ai edge case where the last delta and stop arrive in the same flush — I parse on stop regardless of whether a trailing delta was seen, which covers it. Adding a test for exactly that ordering.
Running the copilot tests to confirm streaming + the tool-arg assembly.

Provider stays behind lib/ai.ts so the Anthropic→OpenAI swap is a one-line config change, and the delta+stop ordering is covered by a test.
